question: Which small changes to an extent-gated gravity-arc residence law most affect galaxy rotation, cluster lens morphology, and Solar-System screening?

law.interpretation: q is a universal path-residence strength; alpha is accumulation; zeta*Rb is the apogee/saturation scale; n is the high-acceleration screen

galaxy_test.nuisance_policy: Use the fixed-RAR inner-fitted baryonic, distance, and inclination nuisances unchanged for every arc variant
galaxy_test.universal_q_fit: Fit one q to all inner points using equal-galaxy mean squared velocity error; never fit q per galaxy
galaxy_test.mass_radius_control: Rb=sqrt(G*Mproxy/a0), which exposes whether the fit requires the same square-root mass normalization underlying deep-MOND/RAR scaling

cluster_shape_test.interpretation: Same-data descriptive replay against normalized standard-GR kappa maps; it ranks geometry changes but cannot validate the kernel or its absolute q

solar_test.limitation: First-order force and perihelion proxies, not a multi-planet ephemeris or derived PPN calculation

claim_limits: The formula family and extent gate were proposed after viewing the ten cluster maps, so all rankings are exploratory.
SPARC uses fixed nuisances inherited from RAR rather than independently refitting each arc variant; this isolates formula response but is not a final likelihood comparison.
The galaxy R50/R80 values are force-equivalent baryonic profile proxies within the observed radial range.
Cluster tests use normalized reconstructed kappa morphology and do not determine absolute lensing strength.
Solar checks impose zero gravitational slip and are phenomenological proxies.
